messages:
incident-bot: [AUTO-PAGE] autopager triggered for service=runtime-canary region=us-west-2; symptom=5xx-rate  threshold=5% for 3m; pd_incident=PD12345 :rotating_light:
pagerduty: Incident PD12345 created; summary=Canary 5xx spike — us-west-2; urgency=high; runbook=/runbooks/canary-5xx.md
alice: acked PD12345 :white_check_mark: I’m oncall. looking at logs now.
alice: quick healthcheck — p95 latency up, 5xxs are mostly 504 gateway timeouts; traffic to canary pods only.
michael: @alice seeing same. canary rollout v2.3.7 started ~5m before spike. suspect cache invalidation job that ran as post-deploy hook.
eva: assigning monitoring panels -> dashboard shows error-rate jump at 15:24:12, pods with pod-restarts=0, cpu ok. KV cache miss rate jumped x10.
alice: pinging support — @sara can we surface customer reports? any big customers impacted?
sara: support: a few enterprise integrations reported failed requests in the last 10m, correlation id present. no outage pages from customers yet, but some error alerts.
michael: grabbing canary pod logs: ```
[2026-03-15T15:24:12Z] WARN kv_cache: eviction job started
[2026-03-15T15:24:12Z] ERROR handler: upstream request timed out after 10s
[2026-03-15T15:24:13Z] ERROR router: failed to retrieve prefix_kv for tenant=acme-corp
```
alice: that lines up. post-deploy hook ran eviction; looks like eviction cleared warm caches causing high backend load and stalls -> 504s.
michael: repro locally with canary image + eviction flag, saw spike. mitigation options: 1) revert canary (rollback), 2) patch hook to no-op eviction on canary, 3) divert traffic to stable.
eva: ops recommendation: immediate traffic diversion + revert canary. divert is fastest to stop customer impact.
alice: doing divert now -> running command: ```
# route traffic 100% -> stable
redwoodctl rollout traffic --service runtime --target stable --region us-west-2
```
incident-bot: action acknowledged: traffic reroute job submitted (job_id=job-9987).
alice: traffic divert in progress — SDKs showing error rate dropping in the canary target and stable ramping to full traffic. p50 latencies normalizing. :thumbsup:
michael: initiating rollback for deployment v2.3.7 in us-west-2: ```
kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deployment/runtime-canary --to-revision=5
```
incident-bot: PD12345 update: rollback started by michael.
sara: notifying affected customers with templated note: "We observed transient errors for requests in us-west-2 around 15:24 UTC. A canary release triggered an internal cache eviction; traffic has been reverted to stable. We're investigating root cause and will follow up."
tom: product: can we confirm if feature flag for eviction was enabled by default in release? need to prevent future auto-eviction on canary.
michael: confirmed — the hook reads FEATURE_EVICT_ON_DEPLOY=true by default. will file immediate PR to gate it behind RELEASE_STAGE!=canary.
eva: alerting: suppress autopager for same symptom for 10m to avoid noise while we verify.
alice: monitoring shows 5xx back down to baseline ~2m after divert. beginning post-incident checks. assigning action items:
- michael: PR to gate eviction on canary + add safety check (due by EOD)
- eva: alert threshold tuning to add canary-specific suppression (due by EOD)
- sara: customer followups and timeline (ongoing)
- oliver: please take final verification and oncall handoff in 30m.
oliver: taking handoff at 16:00 UTC. reading up. :eyes:
incident-bot: PD12345 status: acknowledged -> resolved candidate; oncall confirms stability required for close.
alice: marking incident as mitigated. will keep thread open until rollback confirmed and PR created. thanks all for quick responses. :coffee:
michael: pushed rollback completed on replicasets; canary image replaced. log snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T15:29:40Z] INFO rollout: undo complete, new-revision=5
[2026-03-15T15:29:41Z] INFO router: traffic now at stable=100% region=us-west-2
```
sara: customer notification sent; a few replies asking for postmortem.
alice: will schedule incident review and postmortem doc. tagging @tom for prioritization.
tom: noted — want root-cause, timeline, and compensating controls. assign to michael + eva.
oliver: taking oncall handoff now. if anything else pops, ping me.
incident-bot: PD12345 closed by alice at 16:03 UTC after runbook checks passed. :white_check_mark:
